description.narrative:
The Mekong Inclusive Water Governance and Climate Resilience Program aims to achieve Resilient, Inclusive, and Sustainable Development of the Mekong Subregion through more inclusive transboundary water resource governance and climate resilience. An estimated 80% of the nearly 65 million people living in the Lower Mekong River Basin depend on the major rivers, and their watersheds and floodplains. These rivers drive ecosystems supporting global biodiversity; provide food and income; trade routes and environmental services.However, these transboundary rivers are under threat from uncoordinated largescale development, unsustainable resource extraction, ill-conceived infrastructure and climate change. There is inadequate attention to social and ecological impacts; minimal attention to cumulative impact across these developments, across national boundaries and over time; and minimal engagement with the riverine communities most affected by these developments. In particular, there is little attention to the perspectives and voices of most-affected community members including women, Indigenous People, youth, and People with Disability further contributing to social marginalisation.
This Program addresses the above issues by promoting inclusive and coordinated approaches to transboundary water resource development and climate resilience that elevates the voices of riverine communities, especially women and Indigenous People, who are disproportionately affected by large scale river resource development and the intensifying climate crisis. This is achieved through strategic partnerships with an estimated 30 local, national, and regional Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) across the Mekong Subregion including community organisations, academic/think tanks and networks/coalitions promoting the interests of riverine communities, women, youth, People with Disability and Indigenous People. Through technical, financial and accompaniment support and a convening/facilitation approach, Oxfam will support these partners to engage with state actors, the private sector and inter-governmental bodies at multiple levels to advocate for more inclusive and effective water and climate-related policies, programs and mechanisms. Theprogram’s three thematic pillars align closely to the Mekong Australia Partnership Phase 2 (MAP2) End of Portfolio Outcome 3. increasing the leadership and economic opportunities for women, People with Disability and other marginalised groups; 2. promoting management of water resources in a more coordinated and sustainable way; and 1. reducing vulnerability of riverine communities to the impacts of climate change. Promotion of Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) through inclusive women’s leadership isboth a specific program outcome area and contributes directly to the program thematic pillars of 2. Improved Water Resource Governance and 3. Climate Resilience
The key beneficiaries will be selected riverine communities across the Mekong Subregion; women and community leaders; CSOstaff and members of networks; academics and researchers; and staff of targeted government agencies, regional bodies and private sector actors who will participate in community demonstration sites, learning and dialogue events, workshops and conferences.
The impact of this work is the increased ability of inclusive civil society to play leadership roles in influencing policies, programs and mechanisms that provide economic opportunity and promote climate resilience; and the adoption of policies, programs and processes that result in more inclusive, sustainable development outcomes for transboundary rivers, and the communities that rely on them directly and indirectly.
Planned activities include:
Pillar 1. GEDSI and Feminist Influencing:
Community research including Thai/Sao Baan/villager, Community Action Research, and Feminist Participatory Action Research supported by academic and CSO partners to empower communities and provide alternative information/data to the general public and decisionmakers.
Linking and networking between community researchers nationally and regionally to form advocacy coalitions/alliances.
Support organisations representing and/or promoting the rights and leadership of women, People with Disability and Indigenous People to advance more inclusive WRG and climate actions.
Broker safe spaces for participation, representation and leadership of women and representatives of marginalised social groups in WRG and Climate Resilience dialogue events at all levels. Thisincludes network building/strengthening, tailored learning, preparatory meetings and convening of dialogue events and facilitation of participation in dialogue events convened by others.
Continued support for feminist networks of marginalised socialgroups including psycho-social counselling and unpaid care roles.
Promote increased use of GEDSI analysis at all levels including GEDSI Impact Assessment among partners and stakeholders.
Regional networking and exchange between women leaders includingthe Women and Rivers Congress and the Network of Indigenous Women in Asia.
Pillar 2. Water Resource Governance (WRG):
Support (funding and capacity strengthening) to diverse CSOs and networks (established and emerging) at sub-national, nationalandregional levels engaged in WRG.
Support riverine communities including community-basedfisheries and water resource management groups, to undertake planning, learning and awareness raising, engage with authorities, water resource management activitiesandtransboundary river sub-basin to sub-basin learning and peer support exchanges.
Support consistent CSO participation in WRG dialogue events at all levels to promote long-term acceptance of inclusive approaches. This includes learning events, preparatory meetings and convening of dialogue events or support to participate in events convened by other stakeholders. Key WRG issues include planned water development projects, and related laws and policies at multiple levels including on GEDSI,social, and environment impact assessment and policies on water infrastructure.
Support national and regional networks and coalitions including secretariat services, regular meetings, development of policy positions, participation in external events and linking between networks at all levels.
Use of diverse media to create and mobilise public awareness of key issues targeting youth and other social segments.
Pillar 3. Climate Resilience:
Facilitate community organisation and capacity strengthening related todisaster risk management/climate resilience for CSOs and riverine communities.
Promote the voice of women, Indigenous People, People with Disability and other marginalised groups in climate and economic resilience policy and practice through researchand analysis and convened dialogue events and those supported by others.
Facilitate community vulnerability mapping and disaster/climate risk scenario management activities linked to sub national disaster risk management structures.
Facilitate accessto actionable hydro-meteorological data and technical support (consultants, government agencies and other CSOs).
Support linkages between communities and sub-nationaland national disaster management and WRG structures including early warning systems.
Pilot inclusive community climate resilient livelihood projects, documentation and facilitate the exchange and dissemination of experience.
Program Partners: include an estimated 30 CSO partners such as community organisations, Women Rights Organisations; Indigenous People organisations, national and international CSOs; networks and coalitions; and research institutions. The partner portfolio will be a mix of well-established and new partners that work towards at least one but mostly across all Program pillars. Partners will be responsible for implementation of planned activities supported and coordinated by Oxfam. The specific partners will be finalised during the program inception period. Oxfam’s well-established partner management systems incorporate due diligence, flexibility and capacity support and balances the integrity of each partner’s own approaches with common standards and compliance.
Stakeholders: include government and inter-governmental bodies and private sector actors involved inWRG and climate resilience (such as the Mekong River Commission (MRC), water resource ministries and national/multilateral banks); other related programs include those implemented by other agencies such as the Australian Water Partnership, the StimpsonCentre, World Wildlife Fund, International Union for Conservation of Nature, MONASH University; otherprograms implemented by Oxfam such as Fair Finance Asia; Influencing Just Energy Transition in ASEAN and Transboundary Rivers of South Asia; andother partnerswithin MAP2. This Program will facilitate diverse civil society engagement including learning/analysis, active participation of women and civil society leaders and access to field sites/communities for dialogue, consultations and activities of these stakeholders. Coordination and engagement opportunities will be planned through the Program Steering Committee that includes DFAT/MAP2 representation and through the network of actors engaged in WRG developed over the past 10 years.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project#s implementation.
